sections.h2: Which sale route is quickest in Garland?
sections.html:
A cash sale is quickest, a listing takes longest, and selling on your own sits between. The house's condition and whether tenants live in it should drive the choice.

Garland has its own Code Compliance Department, which runs a permit program for single-family and short-term rentals. For a rental house, that program affects a sale more than any market swing. An investor can buy as-is and handle the permit change, while a retail buyer expects an inspected, move-in ready home.

  • Cash sale: no showings or repair haggling, with a closing day you pick.
  • Listing: more buyers see it, and you carry prep and inspection requests.
  • Owner sale: you manage the contract, disclosures and title work.

sections.h2: What does Garland require of rental houses I want to sell?
sections.html:
Garland requires every single-family rental, duplexes included, to hold a permit from Code Compliance. The city's program page says the permit cannot be assigned or transferred, so a buyer who keeps renting must apply in their own name.

Garland rental permit terms as printed on the city program page
ItemWhat the page says
Single-family rental annual fee$65 on the page, with the renewal fee rising to $250 from Oct. 1, 2026
Short-term rental annual fee$500, with a floor plan and proof of insurance
Single-family inspectionFull inspection at each change of tenancy, unless the property is certified
Short-term inspectionAnnual inspection for renewal
TransferPermit cannot be assigned or transferred

The same page states that the city council was considering an ordinance to treat short-term rentals as a distinct land use, generally allowed by right only in Light Commercial and Heavy Commercial districts and in planned development districts that expressly allow it. A public hearing was set for October 20, 2026. Because that date has passed, call Code Compliance at 972-485-6400 to learn whether the ordinance was adopted and whether it affects your address.

sections.h2: Can code violations stop a Garland sale?
sections.html:
Yes. Code violations do not stop a sale, but they can cut buyer interest and need to be disclosed to anyone who asks. A cash buyer is often the easier choice because the house is bought as-is.

If you have received a notice of violation and need more time, the city tells owners to contact their Code Compliance Officer. The department also accepts requests through its online portal and the eAssist app, and its phone line is 972-485-6400. A short extension in writing is useful to hand a buyer along with the notice.

  • Keep a copy of every notice and any extension.
  • Ask the officer what a reinspection would require.
  • Tell the title company about open violations before the contract is signed.

sections.h2: How do unpaid taxes complicate a Garland sale?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax stays with the property. A lien attaches every January 1, and no buyer gets clear title until what is owed has been paid.

Bills go out around October 1 and turn delinquent after January 31. Penalty and interest start accruing the next day, with the penalty reaching 12 percent by July 1 and a unit's collection attorney able to add up to 20 percent more.

Relief may exist. Some collectors offer installment plans of up to 36 months on a homestead, and penalty relief can be requested in writing if you act within the printed deadlines. Ask the office that bills your Garland parcel for its payoff and plan terms.

sections.h2: What happens if my Garland taxes go to a tax sale?
sections.html:
A constable or an agent of the taxing unit auctions the property, and no statewide list exists. County clerk and tax office websites are where notices appear.

Former owners of homestead, farm or mineral property may buy it back for two years after the purchaser's deed is filed, paying a 25 percent premium in year one or 50 percent in year two, along with the bid and costs. Other property carries a 180-day window. Surplus sale money can be claimed for two years.

A sale you close first spares you that process. Request a current payoff, and ask whether suit has been filed.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Garland house I inherited?
sections.html:
Start by documenting who owns it. Heirs not named on a recorded deed must give the appraisal district an ownership affidavit, a death certificate and a recent utility bill before claiming a homestead exemption.

A recorded transfer on death deed passes the property without probate, and a Lady Bird deed lets the owner sell without the beneficiary's consent. Without either, ask the county clerk about probate filings and small estate affidavits.

Heirs often prefer not to repair and list a house they do not live in, which makes a documented as-is cash sale a common choice.

sections.h2: What should a Garland rental buyer agree to?
sections.html:
Ask who will apply for the new permit, who pays for any inspection, and how existing tenants will be treated. Those three answers decide whether the closing runs smoothly.

  • Whether the offer is as-is, including any items the city inspection might flag.
  • Whether the buyer takes over the lease and the security deposit, or needs the house vacant.
  • Who covers the permit fee and the inspection at the change of tenancy.
  • What the closing date is and which title company will handle the funds.

Put every answer in the written contract. If the house is a short-term rental, also confirm that the buyer understands the annual inspection and insurance steps the city lists for renewal.

sections.h2: What if someone is living in my Garland house without a lease?
sections.html:
An owner may be able to ask the sheriff or constable for removal without a lawsuit, but only when specific conditions are met. Texas Property Code chapter 24B covers this, and the State Law Library eviction guide summarizes it.

  • The occupant stayed after being told to leave.
  • The property was not open to the public when the occupant entered.
  • No lawsuit is pending between you and the occupant.
  • The occupant is not a family member or a current or former tenant.

A wrongful removal can bring a lawsuit against the owner, so confirm each condition first. Someone who was a tenant needs the ordinary eviction process in justice court instead. Either way, tell any buyer about the occupant in writing, since a cash buyer may take the house occupied while a retail buyer will not.

sections.h2: What steps finish a Garland closing?
sections.html:
A deed is filed at the clerk's office for the county that holds the parcel, after the seller's signature is acknowledged before a notary or similar officer. Recording charges vary, so request the total from the clerk or title company.

If a foreclosure notice is pending, its sale date is a hard deadline: the notice must be posted and filed at least 21 days beforehand. Aim to close well ahead of that date.

faqs.q: Can a Garland rental permit transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The city's program page says the permit cannot be assigned or transferred, so the buyer applies in their own name if they will rent the house.

faqs.q: Did Garland adopt the new short-term rental rules?
faqs.a: A hearing was set for October 20, 2026. Call Garland Code Compliance at 972-485-6400 to learn the outcome and whether it affects your address.

faqs.q: What is the annual Garland single-family rental permit fee?
faqs.a: The city page printed $65 a year, with renewals rising to $250 beginning October 1, 2026. Short-term rental permits were printed at $500 a year.

faqs.q: When do Garland property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: A bill still open after January 31 is late, and charges begin the next day.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Garland house before a tax foreclosure auction?
faqs.a: Yes. Paying the taxes from closing proceeds clears the lien, and finishing ahead of an auction sidesteps redemption rules and added court costs.
